My forecast reflects a nuanced expectation for the value over different time horizons. The widening of the 90% confidence intervals across the time horizons directly corresponds to increasing uncertainty as we look further into the future. For the one-day forecast, the interval is relatively tight, [171.81, 182.8], reflecting that most variables are expected to remain stable over such a short period. As the forecast extends to one week, and especially to one month with an interval of [155.15, 204.87], the potential for various influencing factors to shift or emerge grows significantly. Key sources of this increased uncertainty include inherent market volatility, the possibility of new economic data or policy changes, and the compounding effect of minor fluctuations over extended periods, all of which broaden the range of plausible outcomes.

While my forecast outlines the most probable trajectory and a reasonable range of outcomes, specific risks or unforeseen events could push actual results outside these stated intervals. On the upside, a sudden positive economic shock, a major policy change boosting confidence, or an unexpected technological advancement relevant to the underlying asset could drive the value significantly higher than anticipated. Conversely, a sharp economic downturn, a significant geopolitical event, a supply chain disruption, or unforeseen regulatory headwinds could trigger a substantial decline, pushing the value well below the lower bound of my predictions. These high-impact, difficult-to-predict events represent the primary external risks to the accuracy of the confidence intervals.
